story_type: Guard trucks and boat crews drive into floodwater after levees fail
hook: The levees failed. So the Army drove straight into the flood.
narration: The levees failed, so the Army drove straight into the flood.
In December twenty twenty five, rivers overtopped their banks and levees failed across western Washington.
About three hundred Guard soldiers and airmen mobilized to help first responders.
In Burlington, hundreds of homes were ordered to evacuate right away.
Tall military trucks can ford water that would stall a car, so they can carry people out after the roads go under.
Boat crews pushed out across the brown water to reach anyone stranded.
[short pause] After dark, crews waded out to a car caught in the water and helped a person into a raft.
outcome: In one week, the Guard supported five swift water rescues, helped with thirty seven evacuations and made one hoist rescue.
title: Army trucks drive into a flood
description:
Washington National Guard members respond to floods in Skagit, Snohomish and King counties, Washington, Dec. 11-19, 2025, helping first responders with rescues and evacuations.

extra_sources.excerpt: As rivers overtopped banks and levees failed across western Washington, the Washington National Guard launched one of its largest and fastest flood responses in recent memory, mobilizing approximately 300 soldiers and airmen to help first responders with emergency rescues, evacuations, and levee reinforcement in Skagit, Snohomish, and King counties from Dec. 11-18, 2025.
In the city of Burlington, hundreds of homes were under Level 3 (Go Now!) evacuation orders, and the Skagit River levee near Lyman and Concrete remained fragile.

During the one-week mission, Guard members filled more than 20,000 sandbags, manned numerous traffic control points, supported five swift water rescues, assisted with 37 evacuations, and conducted one hoist rescue mission, saving a resident whose vehicle was swept away near the Skagit River.
